'''Hikosashima-no-Ōkimi''' (''hikosashima-ō''{{Sfn|Hikosashima-no-Ōkimi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}; in {{ill|kyūjitai|ja|旧字体|lt=traditional kanji}}, {{lang|ja|彥狹島王}}; dates of birth and death unknown) was a member of the {{ill|imperial family|ja|皇族|lt=royal family}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} as transmitted in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'' and other sources. He is said to have been the first '''{{ill|Kamitsukenu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}}'''.

A grandson of {{ill|Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} (prince of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}) and father of {{ill|Mimorowake-no-Ōkimi|ja|御諸別王}}. The ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'' writes "Hikosashima-no-Ōkimi"; other sources also write '''{{ill|Hikosashima-no-Mikoto|ja|彦狭島命}}''' (see [[#Analysis|below]]).

== Records ==
According to the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'', Emperor Keikō, year 55, second month, Hikosashima-no-Ōkimi was appointed governor of the fifteen provinces of the Tōsandō, but on reaching Anakui-mura in Kasuga he fell ill and died. The people of the eastern provinces grieved and stole his remains away to bury them in {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}}. In the same book, Emperor Keikō year 56, eighth month, his son {{ill|Mimorowake-no-Ōkimi|ja|御諸別王}} took his place to govern the eastern provinces, and their descendants are said to be in the east.

In the {{ill|Kamitsukenu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} entry of the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', it is said that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, when Hikosashima-no-Mikoto — grandson of Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto — first pacified the twelve eastern provinces, he was enfeoffed as kuni no miyatsuko.

The location of "Anakui-mura" mentioned in the ''Nihon Shoki'' is unclear, but one theory identifies it with {{ill|Anabuki Shrine|ja|穴吹神社}} ({{ill|Nara|ja|奈良市|lt=Nara City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}).{{Sfn|Hikosashima-no-Ōkimi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}

== Descendant clans ==
The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}}'' records the following as descendants:
* Kōbetsu, Sakyō, Tarumi-no-Fubito — same kin as the Kamitsukenu clan. Descendants of Hikosashima-no-Mikoto, grandson of Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto.
